findings.title: AndroidManifest.xml XML comment contains illegal double hyphen: all Android builds fail
findings.root_cause: The inline comment wrote `flutter build apk --release`, i.e. `--` inside an XML comment. XML forbids `--` in comments, so AAPT2/ManifestMerger throws SAXParseException and :app:processDebugMainManifest fails. Every Android build (debug and release) was broken.
findings.proposed_fix: Reword the comment so no `--` sequence appears.
findings.applied_fix: Replaced `flutter build apk --release` with `flutter build apk` (release) in the comment.
findings.verification: flutter build apk --debug -> exit 0, 'Built build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-debug.apk'. Before: exit 1 with ManifestMerger2$MergeFailureException / SAXParseException lineNumber 4.

findings.title: Truncated test file: admin customer-directory test has no main(), leaving the suite red and the documented regression unguarded
findings.root_cause: The file contains imports, a detailed regression doc comment and mock/fake scaffolding but no main() and no tests. dart test reports 'Failed to load ... Missing definition of main method'. The same file produced all 4 baseline flutter analyze warnings (unused imports). The regression it documents (profiles.email -> PostgREST 42703) therefore had zero coverage.
findings.proposed_fix: Reconstruct main() with tests that (a) assert fetchCustomers requests exactly `id, full_name, phone, membership_tier` (stub matches exact column list, so re-adding `email` fails the test), maps rows and degrades failures, and (b) assert getOrderDetails goes through the admin-checked get_order_details RPC, reshapes the payload, and degrades null/throw paths.
findings.applied_fix: Reconstructed main() with 5 tests plus a _FakeRpcBuilder helper; mocktail stubs use thenAnswer for builder-returning calls.
findings.verification: flutter test test/features/admin/data/admin_customer_directory_test.dart -> 5/5 pass; flutter analyze -> No issues found (4 warnings eliminated).

findings.title: App-lock tests never provided a Directionality ancestor: 8/8 tests failed
findings.root_cause: The harness pumped AppLockGate with a raw Scaffold child directly under pumpWidget. Flutter requires a Directionality ancestor for Scaffold (normally supplied by MaterialApp), so every test threw 'No Directionality widget found' and the whole app-lock file was red. The widget itself is correct in production (it sits above/inside MaterialApp).
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the pumped tree in MaterialApp in the harness helper and in the one inline pumpWidget call.
findings.applied_fix: wrap() now returns MaterialApp(home: AppLockGate(...)); the second test wraps its inline pump the same way.

findings.title: App-lock sign-out escape caught only Exception, so a thrown Error crashed the lock screen instead of staying fail-closed
findings.root_cause: _signOut used `on Exception catch (e)`. The widget's documented contract is that a failed sign-out keeps the app locked (the escape must never become a bypass). A thrown Error (e.g. StateError) is not an Exception, so it escaped `unawaited(signOut())`, becoming an unhandled async error and crashing the lock screen. Same class of bug the repository elsewhere guards against with broad catches.
findings.proposed_fix: Catch Object (not just Exception) at this boundary, log it, and return without unlocking.
findings.applied_fix: `on Object catch (e)` with an explanatory comment; lock state untouched on failure.
findings.verification: test 'a failing sign-out keeps the app locked (no bypass)' passes; test asserts child stays hidden and the lock title is shown.

findings.title: PaymentStatusWatcher never closed its StreamController on unsubscribe
findings.root_cause: watch() creates a StreamController and cleans up the realtime channel and fallback timer in onCancel, but never closed the controller itself. The controller (and its buffers) therefore survived until GC after every payment watch, instead of being released deterministically at unsubscribe.
findings.proposed_fix: Close the controller in onCancel, guarded by isClosed.
findings.applied_fix: `if (!controller.isClosed) unawaited(controller.close());` added to onCancel; emitTerminal already guards on isClosed.
findings.verification: flutter analyze clean; flutter test test/features/payments -> all payment tests pass (105).

findings.title: dart format drift across 7 files (4 first-party lib files)
findings.root_cause: Files were edited without running dart format, so `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` exited 1. This makes any formatter gate in CI red and adds avoidable diff noise.
findings.proposed_fix: Run dart format over lib and test.
findings.applied_fix: dart format lib test applied (7 files changed).

findings.title: Stale TODO claiming cached_network_image still needs adding
findings.root_cause: The TODO references work already delivered: every remote product image renders through ProductImageResolver / AppImage, which wrap CachedNetworkImage (see their doc comments). A stale TODO misdirects future readers into re-implementing existing behaviour.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the TODO and note where caching actually lives.
findings.applied_fix: TODO replaced with a pointer to ProductImageResolver / AppImage.
findings.verification: flutter analyze clean; storefront tests pass.

findings.title: Admin customer directory is filtered by RLS because the referenced 061 policy migration does not exist
findings.root_cause: profiles grants only auth.uid() = id (migration 002). The admin directory therefore returns just the caller's own row: no data is leaked, but the screen silently under-reports. Repository comments reference supabase/migrations/_proposals/061_admin_profiles_read.sql, which is absent from the repo, so the gap has no reviewable artifact.
findings.proposed_fix: Ship the review-gated SQL proposal adding a SELECT policy for admins (is_admin) on public.profiles, and require human review before supabase db push.
findings.applied_fix: Route (a) chosen and executed by the owner (commit 445d3fa): supabase/migrations/061_admin_profiles_read.sql now exists as a real migration with provenance notes citing the auditor proposal. Applied to the LIVE databases on owner instruction ('do all', 2026-09-15) via the Management API SQL endpoint: staging (zvpjngdgbpnkkqrorkul) then production (alxwvyflasewslinufqe); recorded in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations as version 61 on both.
findings.verification: Staging behavioural RLS proof: admin sub -> 25/25 rows visible; non-admin sub -> exactly 1 (own). Production applied identically (pre-apply snapshot of profiles policies kept for rollback); production non-admin probe -> 1 (own) — production has ZERO is_admin profiles, so the admin path activates as soon as the owner promotes an admin there (owner-only decision). Helper is SECURITY DEFINER on both. Admin Customers screen eyeball on a device remains the owner's final sign-off.

findings.title: Unpinned dependency constraint `http: any` in dev_dependencies
findings.root_cause: `http: any` accepts any future major version, so a fresh `flutter pub get` can silently pull a breaking release into the test harness; it also bypasses the deliberate pinning discipline the rest of pubspec documents.
findings.proposed_fix: Pin to `http: ^1.2.0` (compatible with the current lock) or remove the dependency if unused.
findings.applied_fix: Owner action (commit 48462d9): pubspec.yaml now pins `http: ^1.2.0`. Gates re-proven on the merge head after the pin.
findings.verification: flutter pub outdated shows no security-relevant flags; the change is a one-line edit pending owner sign-off.

findings.title: Documented TODO requires a schema field to resolve (catalog colour names)
findings.root_cause: catalogColorName maps hardcoded ARGB ints to display names; the code's own TODO(audit) notes the correct fix is a Product.colorName column. That is a DB/schema decision, not a code-only change.
findings.proposed_fix: Add products.color_name (or a colours lookup table) and read it through the mapper, keeping the 'Other' fallback.
findings.applied_fix: Implemented (commit 6256c80): migration 062_products_color_name.sql adds products.color_name text (both DBs applied, history v62); Product.colorName (nullable) added to the entity, mapped by ProductCodec.fromRow and round-tripped by encode/decode; the catalogColorName tint map stays as the documented fallback.
findings.verification: flutter analyze 0 issues; flutter test 890/890 (2 new AUD-011 tests: fromRow maps color_name, mistyped/absent degrades to null, encode/decode round-trip + legacy-cache decode).

findings.root_cause: The admin console and the invoice document deliberately bypass l10n.
findings.proposed_fix: If Arabic-speaking staff use the console, add ARB keys and switch to context.l10n; the invoice PDF needs locale plumbing into the builder (currently brand document copy).

findings.title: .gitignore lists lib/generated/ while those generated l10n files are tracked
findings.root_cause: lib/generated/ and *.g.dart are ignored, but the three generated l10n files are committed (so CI can build without running codegen). The ignore rule cannot apply to already-tracked files, so the two rules contradict and future generated files may surprise contributors.
findings.proposed_fix: Either document the exception next to the ignore rule ('l10n output is intentionally tracked') or add a negation pattern (!lib/generated/l10n/).
findings.applied_fix: Fixed (commit 8d8520b): the 'Generated' section now documents the exception — *.g.dart/*.freezed.dart stay untracked, and lib/generated/ (flutter gen-l10n output) is intentionally tracked with regeneration byte-stable via flutter gen-l10n. The contradictory lib/generated/ ignore line was removed.
findings.verification: git ls-files lib/generated -> 3 tracked files; git check-ignore confirms they are no longer shadowed by an ignore rule.

findings.title: Tracked staging config file contains a real committed Supabase anon JWT (placeholders were the documented convention)
findings.root_cause: .gitignore documents the convention that the committed templates (env.staging.json / env.production.json) hold PLACEHOLDERS and real values live in the gitignored *.local.json variants. env.production.json honours this (REPLACE_WITH_*), but env.staging.json holds a genuine 208-character JWT (3 segments, decodes to role=anon, iss=supabase, far-future exp). It entered the tree with commit d50a181 ('refactor(security): implement environment isolation and harden payment flows'). A Supabase anon key is public-by-design and RLS-gated, so there is no direct exploit path - the risk is the breached convention plus reliance on RLS completeness, and it was missed by the 2026-09-14 live-DB check (which only cleared env.production.json).
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the value in the tracked template with a placeholder (mirroring env.production.json), keep the real key only in gitignored config/env.staging.local.json, and rotate the staging anon key in the Supabase dashboard if the project treats it as sensitive. Because the key is in git history, rotation - not just removal - is the durable fix.
findings.applied_fix: Owner action (commit ebe381b): the tracked template now holds the placeholder REPLACE_WITH_STAGING_ANON_KEY. Final round (owner 'disable legacy keys', 2026-09-15): the Management API has no per-key legacy rotation endpoint, so the documented migration was completed instead — the project's provisioned sb_publishable_ key was placed in gitignored config/env.staging.local.json and .env.staging (REST-verified 200 while both key families coexisted), then legacy JWT keys were disabled via API PUT /v1/projects/{ref}/api-keys/legacy?enabled=false. End-to-end safety proof executed before and after: an edge-function probe (cancel-expired-orders) and a real authenticated delete-account round-trip returned 200 {deleted:true} POST-disable, proving the platform swaps the managed SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY env for edge functions on its own (a user-secret override is impossible - the name is platform-reserved, HTTP 400).
findings.verification: Post-disable REST probes: legacy anon JWT -> 401 (enforcement landed ~2 min after the flip; the leaked 208-char JWT from d50a181 is now REJECTED), legacy service_role -> 401, sb_publishable_ key -> 200, edge function -> 401 scheduler-mismatch (healthy, not 503). A throwaway staging user was signed up with the publishable key and fully deleted through the payment-critical service-client path as the end-to-end proof. Production (alxwvyflasewslinufqe) legacy keys intentionally untouched (its anon key was never leaked); parity migration can follow the same path later.

findings.title: Corrupt/unsorted .git/packed-refs breaks git clone of the repository (CI and onboarding blocker)
findings.root_cause: While verifying the audit, `git clone --local` of the repository failed with 'fatal: multiple updates for ref refs/heads/audit-remediation not allowed', and git fsck reported 'packed-refs line 10: packedRefUnsorted: refname refs/heads/audit-remediation is less than previous refname refs/heads/mostafasayed118/chore/bump-all-pub-dependencies'. The packed-refs file is no longer sorted, and the same ref also exists as a loose ref with a different SHA (447f645 vs the packed 83fc99c), so git sees two conflicting definitions. HEAD reflog also contains invalid entries. A fresh clone, a CI checkout, or a new worktree of this repository therefore fails. Not caused by the audit - discovered by it.
findings.proposed_fix: Back up .git/packed-refs, then restore a consistent ref store: remove the duplicate/stale entry, re-sort the file (keeping the '# pack-refs with: peeled fully-peeled sorted' header), and run `git pack-refs --all` followed by `git fsck --full` to confirm. Decide which SHA is the real audit-remediation tip before deleting either definition, and consider dropping the stray refs/heads/mostafasayed118/* branch that a PR-ref mapping appears to have created.
findings.applied_fix: Owner action: the stale duplicate packed entry (83fc99c) was removed, keeping the real tip 447f645; backup retained at .git/packed-refs.bak. Verified by the auditor: git show-ref now lists the ref once, and `git clone --local --no-hardlinks . <dir>` exits 0.
findings.verification: Reproduced twice: `git clone --local --no-hardlinks . <dir>` exits 128 with the 'multiple updates for ref' error; `git fsck` reports the packedRefUnsorted line plus invalid HEAD reflog entries; `git show-ref` lists refs/heads/audit-remediation twice with different SHAs. The working repository itself still functions normally (audit branch tip 92b0cb4, clean tree).
